phase4_expiry_shadow_validation.status: PASS -- LIVE, run 32967117214 job 'Phase 4 - Expiry Boundary Shadow Validation'
phase4_expiry_shadow_validation.detail: POST /api/admin/keys always honors an explicit expires_in_days directly, independent of the global SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRY_ENABLED flag (that flag only gates the separate real-customer-provisioning path in provisionApiKey()) -- so a real expires_at boundary was exercised today with a controlled admin-provisioned key, without needing that flag flipped first. Provisioned one ENTERPRISE key with expires_in_days=0.0008 (~69s, chosen because Cloudflare KV's own expirationTtl -- set from the same value -- rejects anything below 60s), confirmed allowed before the boundary (200), waited 80s, confirmed denied after (401). Expected-vs-actual resolveAuth() decisions matched exactly, 0 unexpected differences -- the comparison Phase 4 itself asks for.
phase4_expiry_shadow_validation.caveat: This proves the expires_at enforcement mechanism itself works correctly. It does NOT prove SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRY_ENABLED=true is safe to flip for the real customer-provisioning path -- that flag change is a distinct, larger-blast-radius production behavior change (every future real signup would get a real expiry instead of null) and is intentionally not bundled into this pass; see subscription_expiry_enabled below.

subscription_expiry_status: STILL FALSE, deliberately not flipped this pass. Phase 4's shadow-validation prerequisite is now genuinely satisfied (see above) -- this is a real change from every prior pass, where Phase 4 itself was BLOCKED_BY_SECRET. But flipping SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRY_ENABLED=true changes real behavior for every future real customer signup (provisionApiKey()'s billingCycle-based path), which is a materially larger and more consequential change than anything else shipped this pass. Per the mission's own NO-REGRESSION / PRODUCTION-FIRST posture and this engagement's established pattern of shipping one bounded, individually-verified change per pass, this is the next concrete follow-up (wrangler.toml [vars] and [env.production.vars], deploy, re-run this same certification workflow to confirm 0 regressions) rather than something to bundle into an already-large workflow-testing PR.
